stances.claim: In CJP's Jan 5 column he exalted the women of ASEAN (led by Malaysian CJ Maimun) transforming and empowering gender parity -- today CJP focuses on seven ladies he has met who, in his humble opinion, are exemplars of empowered women of the Philippine private sector.

Dr. Charo Santos-Concio's keynote address during the inaugural MAP meeting stressed that 'leadership and integrity are intertwined' -- without integrity, leadership becomes self-serving and will not build up an organization; integrity without leadership, though not bad per se, does not result in firm decision-making. She was a campus scholar, beauty queen, multi-awarded actress, and acclaimed corporate executive -- the first female president/CEO of ABS-CBN (2008-2015) -- propelling the network to its height in revenue and reach.

Dr. Lydia Echauz is a Meralco independent director where, as her fellow ID, CJP has marveled at her wit and wisdom -- she also sits as ID of Meralco PowerGen Renewable Energy, Shell Philippines, D&L Industries, and other major corporations, and serves as executive director of the Henry Sy Foundation. A towering figure in Philippine education, she was president of FEU and former dean of De La Salle GSB, widely respected for bridging academia and industry.

Bernadine Siy was elected in 2008 as the first and thus far the only lady president and queen of the Manila Golf Club -- since 1901 the club had been a bastion of masculine pride till 1987 when women were admitted. Bern is also the only woman to chair the board of trustees of Ateneo de Manila; under her guidance, Ateneo will establish a new Riverpark Cavite campus. In the boardrooms of PLDT and JG Summit (among many others), Bern as CJP's fellow ID is 'listened to with respect and awe because she studies the agenda and speaks with distinct eloquence.'

Monette Iturralde-Hamlin graduated summa cum laude from the College of the Holy Spirit, obtained -- as a full scholar and with distinction -- her MBM from AIM, and became an executive at World Executive Digest while teaching part-time at AIM. In 1992 in Hong Kong and 1994 in the Philippines, she founded and still heads TeamAsia -- an award-winning integrated marketing group. An active ICD trustee, Monette 'is a gem waiting to be discovered as a capable and trustworthy ID' -- a much-sought-after public speaker and advocate of women's empowerment and sustainability through podcasts and social media.

Chaye Cabal-Revilla, executive director + EVP + chief finance/risk/sustainability officer of MPIC, is the driving force behind MPIC's meteoric rise -- director in major MPIC subs (Meralco, Maynilad, Metro Pacific Tollways, Metro Pacific Health which runs 29 hospitals) and the only female and only Filipino founding member of the A4S CFO Leadership Network established by King Charles III. Under her stewardship, MPIC partnered with FLP in sponsoring the annual P500,000 ESMEL fellowship for five MBA students.

Tessie Sy-Coson is the eldest of the six Sy siblings who together own the country's largest conglomerate in market cap -- she chairs the nation's largest bank BDO (acclaimed by London-based Brand Finance as the most valuable Philippine brand). Despite her storied achievements and being the nation's wealthiest woman, 'she remains simple, modest, unaffected, and unassuming.' While she readily concurs with FLP's annual search for outstanding law students, she believes we should also look for lawyers who are ethical -- FLP heartily agrees and is now formulating guidelines with her or her companies as FLP's partners.

First Lady Louise Araneta-Marcos is 'a distinguished lawyer of integrity and competence' -- when her husband was elected President, she voluntarily dissolved her formidable MOST law office but remained an active law professor; she is especially proud of West Visayas State University (where she teaches), which obtained a 100% bar passing rate in the last bar exam. An Ateneo alumna who honed postgraduate studies in criminal procedure at NYU, she was recently awarded the BizNews Asia Governance Excellence Award. She shares CJP's philosophy of safeguarding liberty and nurturing prosperity under the rule of law and is an active supporter of FLP's proposed AI-powered Museum for Liberty and Prosperity.

one_paragraph_summary: Following his January 5 piece on the women of ASEAN, Panganiban profiles seven empowered women of the Philippine private sector whom he knows personally: Charo Santos-Concio (former ABS-CBN president and MAP keynote on the leadership-integrity nexus), Lydia Echauz (Meralco ID and former FEU president), Bernadine Siy (first lady president of the 1901-founded Manila Golf Club and Ateneo board chair), Monette Iturralde-Hamlin (AIM scholar and TeamAsia founder), Chaye Cabal-Revilla (Metro Pacific CFO and sole Filipino founding member of King Charles III's A4S CFO Leadership Network), Tessie Sy-Coson (BDO chair and the nation's wealthiest woman, who has called for FLP to also identify ethical lawyers), and First Lady Louise Araneta-Marcos (who dissolved her MOST law office and continues teaching at West Visayas State University, which posted a 100% bar passing rate). The column closes affirming the shared philosophy of safeguarding liberty and nurturing prosperity under the rule of law.
